statement: NVIDIA is testing lower HBM memory configurations for Rubin Ultra accelerators, reportedly as low as 192GB versus a planned 1TB, because of HBM4e supply constraints and qualification delays.
why: Fewer memory bits per accelerator directly reduces HBM content sold per GPU, which is the key swing factor for HBM makers' revenue attach rate to the merchant-GPU ramp.

impact.mechanism: HBM4e supply constraints and qualification delays force a lower memory configuration per accelerator, cutting memory bit volume per GPU shipped and signalling a binding upstream memory bottleneck on the merchant-GPU platform ramp.

evidence.excerpt: Nvidia is testing lower memory configurations for its Rubin Ultra accelerators - reportedly as low as 192GB, down from the planned 1TB - due to HBM4e supply constraints and qualification delays.

confidence.basis: Single secondary outlet relaying reported test configurations; no vendor filing or confirmation, so capped at medium.

dispersion: conflicting same-key reports: magnitude 1 -> 2; sources: 24/7 Wall St.
